How it works

A clear, office-managed process for students. Listings are published only by the VishiTalentHub team.

1

Browse & pick your fit

Search by interest, skill or category. Compare pay, duration and the poster's rating — save favourites with the ♥ to decide later.

2

Apply in one step

Fill a short form on the listing. You instantly get an application reference (like VTH-APP-7K2Q) — keep it for any follow-up.

3

Get help with a token

Stuck anywhere? Chat with the assistant below. It raises a support token (like VTH-8K2Q4Z) and hands you over to WhatsApp with everything pre-filled.

✓

Verified listings only

Visitors cannot post work on this site. Every listing is published by the owner from a private, login-only dashboard, so students only see genuine, checked opportunities.

✓

Have work to offer?

Resume Builder

A good resume gets you shortlisted. Answer a few short questions — about you, the role you want, your skills, education and experience — and the builder writes up a clean one-page resume you can download and attach to your applications.

📄

Build your resume in about 3 minutes

No blank page, no formatting struggle. The builder asks one small set of questions at a time — most fields are optional, so skip anything that doesn't apply and fill it in later.

Made for students — sections for projects, internships, certifications and achievements, so it works even with no job experience yet. Leave the summary blank and the builder drafts one from your answers.

Yours to keep — download the finished resume as a file, or copy it as text into any application form. Applied for a listing here before? Your name, contact and college are filled in for you.

Saved in your browser — your answers are kept in this browser on this device, so closing the tab doesn't lose them. A saved resume auto-fills your future applications here and powers your match scores — and you can clear it anytime. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Owner dashboard

Backend: not connected — local mode

One public site, two experiences. Students browse and apply freely. The owner signs in here to publish listings to the shared board, see every application, and manage support tokens — powered by a free Supabase backend (no Google sign-in servers involved).

Supabase backend — keys connected ✓ · 2 steps left

This site runs on Supabase instead of Firebase — sign-in and data go to Supabase's own servers, not Google's. Done so far: your free project is created and this page is now connected to it with your Project URL and publishable key, so the sign-in form below is live. Two quick steps in your Supabase dashboard are left before the shared board works end to end:

  1. ✓ Project created — your Supabase project is live and this page is connected to it (Project URL + publishable key plugged in).
  2. Add your owner login: in the project, open Authentication → Users → Add user → Create new user. Enter your email and a password, and tick Auto confirm user. That email + password is the login the form below checks. Still to do.
  3. Create the tables & access rules: open SQL Editor → New query, paste the setup SQL below, replace YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL with the email from the step above, and click Run. It creates the listings, applications, tokens and saved-listings tables — public to browse and apply, with posting and the dashboard reserved to your owner login only. Still to do — until this runs, the status pill above will say the tables aren't set up yet.
  4. Then sign in below with your owner email and password — the dashboard (post work, all applications, support tokens) unlocks for your account, and this panel hides itself.
Setup SQL — paste into Supabase → SQL Editor 
-- VishiTalentHub — run once in Supabase: SQL Editor → New query → Run
-- Replace YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL (every place it appears) with your owner login email first.

create table if not exists public.jobs (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  title text not null,
  org text not null,
  cat text, type text, loc text,
  pay int, unit text, dur text,
  openings int default 1,
  deadline text,
  skills text[] default '{}',
  resp text[] default '{}',
  description text,
  img text,
  rating numeric,
  reviews int default 0,
  tier text,
  apps int default 0,
  verified boolean default false,
  created_ms bigint,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table if not exists public.applications (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  ref text, job_id text, title text, org text,
  name text, contact text, college text, link text, pitch text,
  status text default 'Applied',
  user_id uuid,
  created_ms bigint,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table if not exists public.tickets (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  token text, name text, type text, descr text, status text,
  user_id uuid,
  created_ms bigint,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table if not exists public.saves (
  user_id uuid primary key,
  saved jsonb default '{}',
  updated_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table if not exists public.stories (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null,
  detail text,
  text text not null,
  created_ms bigint,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

alter table public.jobs enable row level security;
alter table public.applications enable row level security;
alter table public.tickets enable row level security;
alter table public.saves enable row level security;
alter table public.stories enable row level security;

-- Listings: everyone can read; only the owner can post / edit / delete
create policy "jobs are public to read" on public.jobs
  for select using (true);
create policy "owner manages jobs" on public.jobs
  for all using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL')
  with check (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');

-- Applications: anyone can apply; only the owner can read / manage
create policy "anyone can apply" on public.applications
  for insert with check (true);
create policy "owner reads applications" on public.applications
  for select using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');
create policy "owner updates applications" on public.applications
  for update using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL')
  with check (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');
create policy "owner deletes applications" on public.applications
  for delete using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');

-- Support tokens: anyone can raise one; the owner reads all and
-- updates statuses; a signed-in student can read their own tokens
create policy "anyone can raise a token" on public.tickets
  for insert with check (true);
create policy "owner and raiser read tokens" on public.tickets
  for select using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL' or user_id = auth.uid());
create policy "owner updates tokens" on public.tickets
  for update using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL')
  with check (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');
create policy "owner deletes tokens" on public.tickets
  for delete using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');

-- Saved listings: each signed-in student manages only their own row
create policy "own saves only" on public.saves
  for all using (user_id = auth.uid())
  with check (user_id = auth.uid());

-- Placed-student stories: everyone can read; only the owner can add / edit / delete
create policy "stories are public to read" on public.stories
  for select using (true);
create policy "owner manages stories" on public.stories
  for all using (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL')
  with check (auth.jwt() ->> 'email' = 'YOUR_OWNER_EMAIL');

-- Live updates without reloading (if a line says a table is already
-- in the publication, that's fine — ignore it and keep the rest)
alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.jobs;
alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.applications;
alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.tickets;
alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.stories;

The keys are already plugged in. Once the two steps above are done (owner user added + setup SQL run), this panel hides itself — no further page update needed.

Withdrawal sync SQL — let students withdraw their own applications (run once) 
-- VishiTalentHub withdrawal sync — run once in Supabase: SQL Editor → New query → Run
-- Lets a signed-in student set ONLY their own application's status to
-- 'Withdrawn'. Anonymous (not signed-in) applications are withdrawn on
-- the student's device; the owner still sees every withdrawal there.

create policy "students withdraw own applications" on public.applications
  for update using (user_id = auth.uid())
  with check (user_id = auth.uid() and status = 'Withdrawn');

Frequently asked questions

Quick answers — for anything else, the chat assistant (bottom right) can raise a token for you.

Is VishiTalentHub free for students?

Yes — browsing, saving and applying are always free. If anyone asks you to pay a registration or security fee for a student job, treat it as a scam and report it through the chat assistant.

Who can apply for the listings?

Any student. Some listings suit specific skills (React, Excel, video editing), but posters set no degree or year requirement unless the listing says so. If you're unsure you qualify, open the chat and choose “Check my eligibility”.

How and when do I get paid?

The organisation that posted the work pays you directly — the amount, date and mode (UPI or bank transfer) should be agreed in writing before you start. If a payment goes wrong, raise an issue in the chat: you'll get a token the owner can track.

How do poster ratings and tiers work?

After a gig finishes, students rate the poster. The average shows as stars on every listing, and posters earn tiers — New, Established, Top Poster — from their rating and completed gigs. Ratings on the current sample listings are examples.

Can I post work for my shop, startup or society?

No — visitors cannot post work on this site. Only the VishiTalentHub owner can publish listings, from the owner dashboard after signing in with their owner account — there is no public posting form. If you have work to offer, contact the owner via Chat Support / WhatsApp with the details; if approved, the owner will post it for you.

How does the Resume Builder work?

Open Resume Builder in the menu and tap “Start building my resume”. It asks a few short questions in six small steps — about you, the role you're aiming for, your skills, education, experience/projects and extras like certifications. At the end you get a clean one-page resume on screen: download it as a file (open it in any browser to print or save as PDF) or copy it as text into any application form. It's free, needs no sign-up, and your answers are saved in this browser on this device only — nothing is uploaded — so a saved resume auto-fills your future applications here and powers your match scores. “Clear saved resume” in the builder removes it anytime. If you've already applied for a listing here, your name, contact and college are filled in for you.

How do I track my application?

Every application shows a live status under My applications: Applied → Under review → Shortlisted → Selected. The owner moves it along as they review, so you can watch it progress instead of waiting in the dark. You can also type your application reference (like VTH-APP-7K2Q) into the chat assistant for its current status.

What happens when a listing's deadline passes?

The listing closes itself: it stays on the board clearly marked Closed, the Apply button switches off, and it stops accepting applications — nobody can apply to a dead gig. Use the “Hide closed” filter above the board to skip closed listings. Saved a listing that later closed? Its deadline reminder simply stops.

How do I report a listing, or withdraw an application?

Every listing card and detail view has a ⚑ Report button. Reporting raises a support ticket to the owner — the same ticket system as the chat tokens — with the listing reference attached, and you get a ticket ref (like VTH-XXXXXX) you can track under “My support tokens”. To withdraw, open My applications: each application has a “What I sent” view so you can re-read exactly what you submitted, and a Withdraw button (with a confirm step). Withdrawn applications show as Withdrawn and no longer count toward the listing's applied total.

What does the “% match” on a listing mean?

Once you've built a resume with the Resume Builder, each listing shows a match score based on how its required skills line up with the skills and tools on your resume. It's a guide to where you fit best — not a guarantee — and you can attach that same resume to your application in one tap from the apply form.

Can I get alerts for new gigs and deadlines?

Yes — in My Activity → Alerts & reminders, pick a category and tap “Notify me”: new gigs in that category pop up there with a toast while you browse. Listings you've saved or applied to also get automatic deadline reminders there when they're within 3 days of closing.

How does the support token system work?

Choose “Raise an issue” in the chat, answer three quick questions, and you get a token like VTH-8K2Q4Z. The “Continue on WhatsApp” button then opens a chat to the hub owner with your token and issue pre-written — quote the token in any follow-up so your case is easy to find.
